analysis: The only change in this PR is a docs/architecture/inference.md table row (line 1866) describing how the `stop` parameter is scoped. The supplied units (base lines 2420-2981) are unchanged surrounding documentation; they do not contain the patched line, so I used the patch excerpt to identify the changed content. The row now says Gemma 4 and `<think>` parsers exclude reasoning and tool-call spans from stop matching per request (`ReasoningStopScope`), that the native block engine matches the whole output, and that the reported stop sequence replays the request's scope. The change is documentation-only. It adds no code, endpoints, keys, attestation paths or cache storage changes. Threat model touchpoints are limited. The edit describes stop-string matching, which is related to output integrity and availability (T-010, T-007) and not to confidentiality of A-001 or the prefix-cache threat T-041. It does not alter the TB-002/TB-007 trust boundaries. No regression was identified in the documentation text, and it does not invalidate any threat assumption. The behavior it describes (`ReasoningStopScope`, `EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift`) lives in source files not supplied here, so I could not check whether the docs match the implementation. The docs claim that stop strings cannot match inside reasoning or tool-call spans. A wrong implementation could affect tool-call integrity, but there is no evidence of it in this PR. This is an unverified contract for the next pass, not a finding. The supplied context shows no new attack surface.
